title: Icon construction
summary: How to draw a consistent icon: grid, stroke, shape, detail, solid, and size.

overview.purpose: Before you finish an icon, or a set of icons, review it against these construction rules.
overview.when: You are drawing or reviewing an icon, or a set of icons.
takeaways: Draw on a 24×24 canvas. Keep the graphic in the 20×20 live area. Use the 2dp padding only when the icon needs more weight. Never go past the trim.
Start from the keylines: 18×18 square, 20 circle, 20×16 portrait, 16×20 landscape. Use them as guides, not a forced fit.
Snap to whole pixels. Keep width and height equal.

Use one stroke weight (2dp at 24dp in Material) and the same terminals and corner treatment on every icon. Exterior corners: 2dp radius. Interior corners: square. Do not round strokes that are 2dp or thinner. Do not over-round.
Keep shapes bold, geometric, and front-facing. No perspective, no loose organic forms.
Draw curves with as few Bézier points as possible. Keep them smooth and symmetric, with no bumps.
Keep visual weight, gaps, and detail level even across the set. Use familiar metaphors. Reduce each icon to its essential form.
If a rule makes the icon harder to recognize, prioritize legibility.
Do not turn a line icon into a solid by only filling it. Thicken single strokes outward, closed shapes inward, and turn inner lines into slightly wider gaps. Rebalance weight and spacing.
Design at the real size. Use optical sizes 20, 24, 40, and 48 instead of scaling a 24dp drawing up or down. Correct by eye when the grid looks wrong, but do not skew the geometry.

sections.title: Grid and keylines
sections.intro: For each one that fails, name the icon, the problem, and the fix.

items.title: 24×24 live area
items.fix: It looks cropped, tight, or uneven next to other icons, so pull the drawing back into the 20×20 live area and use the padding only when the icon needs more weight.
items.why: Material keeps icon content in the 20×20 live area of a 24×24 canvas, with 2dp of padding on each side. Do not cross the trim.

items.title: Keylines
items.fix: It looks bigger, smaller, or a different shape than sibling icons, so redraw it on the matching keyline, then adjust if the metaphor needs it.
items.why: Material keylines are an 18×18 square, a 20 circle, a 20×16 portrait rectangle, and a 16×20 landscape rectangle. They are guides, not a forced fit.

items.title: On the pixel
items.fix: It looks soft or stretched, so place every point on a whole pixel and keep the box square.
items.why: Material says X and Y should be integers, and width should equal height, for example 24×24.

sections.title: Stroke and corners
sections.intro: One weight, one corner treatment, on every icon.

items.title: One stroke weight
items.fix: It looks thinner, thicker, or softer than the rest, so set every stroke to the same weight and use the same terminal.
items.why: Material uses a 2dp stroke at 24dp, including curves and angles, with squared terminals.

items.title: Corner radius
items.fix: It looks puffy, melted, or mixed, so use the set’s radius on the silhouette only, leave inner corners square, and do not round thin strokes.
items.why: Material uses a 2dp radius on the silhouette. Interior corners stay square. Do not round strokes that are 2dp wide or less.

sections.title: Shapes and proportions
sections.intro: Bold, flat, and even with the rest of the set.

items.title: Front-facing
items.fix: It looks 3D, sketchy, or off-angle, so flatten it to a straight-on geometric shape.
items.why: Material icons are bold, geometric, and front-facing. Do not tilt them or make them dimensional.

items.title: Even weight
items.fix: It looks heavier, lighter, or more cramped than its neighbors, so even out the gaps and the amount of ink.
items.why: Streamline says the space between parts, and the visual weight, should stay even across the set.

items.title: Simple curves
items.fix: It looks lumpy, or the handles look messy, so delete extra points, use simple arcs, and align handles so the curve stays smooth.
items.why: Lucide says curves should be smooth and as simple as the shape allows, with no extra points or bumps.

sections.title: Detail and metaphor
sections.intro: Only the marks that make the icon recognizable.

items.title: Essential form
items.fix: It looks busy, or two icons mean the same thing in different ways, so remove extra detail and use the familiar symbol.
items.why: Material reduces each icon to its minimal form. Use a widely recognized metaphor.

items.title: Legibility first
items.fix: It follows the style but is hard to recognize, so relax the rule and restore the familiar shape.
items.why: Streamline says if a style rule makes the icon harder to understand, legibility wins.

sections.title: Solid variant
sections.intro: A filled icon is a new drawing, not a filled stroke.

items.title: Line to solid
items.fix: It looks denser, bigger, or more clogged than the line version, so convert it by hand: fill, shift thickness, open the inner gaps, and rebalance.
items.why: Streamline says not to only fill the line icon. Thicken outward or inward, turn inner lines into slightly wider gaps, then rebalance.

sections.title: Sizes and optical correction
sections.intro: Match the size, then correct by eye. Work in the style of the current set. If two rules conflict, choose the option that stays clear at the intended size.

items.title: Optical size
items.fix: It looks too heavy at a large size, or too faint or tight at a small size, so switch to the matching optical size instead of scaling the 24dp artwork.
items.why: Material optical sizes are 20, 24, 40, and 48dp. A 24dp symbol pairs with a 48dp target. Do not only scale the 24dp drawing.

items.title: Optical correction
items.fix: It is centered on the grid but still looks off, or a tight detail is clogged, so shift it until it looks balanced, without warping the geometry.
items.why: Material allows a small optical tweak on the same geometric forms. Do not skew them. A 1.5dp stroke is allowed only when detail will not fit.
